clue.text: Wow! I seem very odd seen from below

indicators.note: odd says the letters of the words before it are to be rearranged into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how peculiar they look to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is the anagram signal working on all of WOW I SEEM VERY; 'very' looks like it modifies 'odd' but is fodder. The definition describes looking up from ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm's-eye view is the perspective from ground level looking upward, the opposite of a bird's-eye view.

clue.text: We used to cover part of a canal — the Grand Union?

parts.note: we'd is short for we would, and would can mean used to
a lock is a gated section of a canal where the water level is raised or lowered

explanation.surface: A boater recalls covering a stretch of the Grand Union Canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand Union is England's longest canal, but the question mark asks for a grand union of two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the state of marriage, which could be called a grand union of two people.

clue.text: A measure effected by 'one who…

definitions.meaning: a straight-edged strip marked in inches or centimetres used for measuring
read on into the next clue: one who governs, a monarch

explanation.surface: A policy is put into effect by someone who governs, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 3 Down: 'one who … governs'. 'effected by' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a straight measuring stick, and a person who rules over a country.

clue.text: … governs ie, strangely enough, a governor

indicators.note: strangely enough says the preceding letters are to be mixed into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, one who governs turns out, oddly, to be a governor.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue 2 Down. 'strangely enough' rearranges GOVERNS IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a monarch, the supreme ruler or governor of a state.

clue.text: Town house

definitions.meaning: a cathedral city in northern England
a royal dynasty of English kings, rivals of Lancaster in the Wars of the Roses

explanation.definitionFit: It names both an English city and the royal family line that ruled in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: American state where girl takes a trip, we hear

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a cruise is a pleasure trip by sea

explanation.surface: In some American state a girl goes on a voyage, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes CRUISE sound like CRUZ. 'American state' suggests the USA but this one is Mexican.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracruz is a state of Mexico on the Gulf coast, and Mexico is in North America.

clue.text: Little by little, a plant appears

parts.note: Eric, or Little by Little is an 1858 Victorian school story by Frederic Farrar, so its subtitle stands for its hero's name

explanation.surface: A plant gradually comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little by little' looks like 'gradually', but is the subtitle of Farrar's famous moralising school novel Eric, or Little by Little.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, a low-growing flowering shrub.

clue.text: Building complex part of defences

definitions.meaning: an arts and residential complex in the City of London
an outer fortification guarding a castle gate or bridge

explanation.definitionFit: The London arts centre takes its name from the medieval watchtower or gate fortification that stood there.

clue.text: To remain united man found heart-breaking

indicators.note: breaking means the word for heart is split open and something is put into it

parts.note: the core is the heart or centre of something
he is a male person

explanation.surface: A man discovered something heartbreaking about staying together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-breaking' reads as one sad word, but 'breaking' makes HE break into CORE; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together and stay unified.

clue.text: Midwife turned back, ran down again

indicators.note: turned back tells the solver to read the whole phrase that follows from right to left

parts.note: to run someone down is to revile them, so ran down again is re-reviled

explanation.surface: A midwife reverses course and knocks someone over a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran down again' gives RE-REVILED, and 'turned back' reverses that whole string. 'ran down' looks like a car accident but means abused verbally.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwife brings babies into the world, delivering them, so she is literally one who delivers.

clue.text: I had a little house somewhere in America

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
HO is the standard abbreviation of house, so a little (shortened) house

explanation.surface: A nostalgic memory of owning a small home somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had' contracts to I'D, and 'little house' signals the abbreviation HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States, so it is a place in America.

clue.text: Planetarium turning your mistake round

indicators.note: turning tells the solver to reverse the pair of words it introduces

parts.note: YR is the common abbreviation of your, as at the end of a letter
to err is to make a mistake
a round shape is the circular letter O

explanation.surface: Someone at a planetarium is told to turn round and correct an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the whole string YR ERR O. 'round' looks like part of the reversal signal but supplies the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system, a mechanical planetarium showing the planets in motion.

clue.text: In other words, disorderly mob struggle for possession

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation of Latin scilicet, meaning namely or that is to say
a rabble is an unruly crowd

explanation.surface: A mob scuffles over something everyone wants to grab.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, short for scilicet ('namely'), is a crossword convention for 'in other words' or 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scramble or grope about frantically, as when people fight to grab something.

clue.text: This country rejected one who sang for 'another

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters for this country are turned round

parts.note: for a British newspaper this country is the UK
a wait was one of a band of street singers and musicians who performed carols at Christmas

explanation.surface: A nation turns down a singer who performed as a stand-in for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for another' hides the definition: the answer is another country. 'one who sang for another' reads as a session singer, but only 'one who sang' is wordplay; waits were old English carol singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuwait is a Gulf state, a nation other than Britain, so it serves as another country.

clue.text: Two sources of water. — how surprising!

indicators.note: Two tells the solver to write the following word twice

parts.note: a well is a shaft sunk to draw water, a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to find two springs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' doubles the word for a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation expresses astonishment, like goodness me.

clue.text: Rounded natural promontory in boat before being loaded with chlorine

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

indicators.note: being loaded with means the word for before is filled with the chemical symbol

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine

explanation.surface: Someone describes a headland as seen from a boat carrying chlorine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like an order instruction for the boat but is the old word ERE. 'promontory' suggests geography but here means a bump on a bone or plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tubercle is a small rounded projection or nodule on a bone, root or skin, a natural protuberance.

clue.text: Sea proved too rough for bug

indicators.note: too rough means the letters are tossed about as by a stormy sea

explanation.surface: The sea turned out too choppy for an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too rough' rearranges SEA PROVED. 'bug' looks like an insect but is the verb to spy on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug a room is to listen in secretly, which is to overhear private conversation.

clue.text: One so apt to stir

indicators.note: stir means to mix around, so the letters of the words before are scrambled

explanation.surface: A thing so well suited to stirring a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' rearranges ONE SO APT; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is the small spoon for stirring sugar into tea, so it is ideally suited to that job.

clue.text: I run down a Manxman, possibly

parts.note: to run someone down is to disparage or defame them

explanation.surface: A motorist confesses to knocking over a man from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run down' looks like a traffic accident but means defame. A Manxman comes from the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman lives on the Isle of Man, so he is one example of someone living on an isle.

clue.text: Persuade popular leader …

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Il Duce, the leader, was the title of Mussolini

explanation.surface: Persuade a popular leader to speak quickly, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Duce is Italian for leader, Mussolini's title. The trailing dots join this clue to 20 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade or prevail on them to act.

clue.text: A site for a road

parts.note: a venue is the place or site where something happens

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a location for a new road.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street, often tree-lined, so it is a kind of road.

clue.text: … to talk fast

definitions.meaning: to put thoughts into words, to state or voice
very quick, as of a train or delivery service

explanation.surface: Continuing 18 Down: a leader is urged to speak rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to voice in words, and the adjective describes a fast train or delivery.

clue.text: Blue feathers found

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathers of a bird
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A blue feather has been discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is not the past of find but the verb to found, to make by pouring metal into a mould. 'Blue' means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel blue is to be sad or dejected, which is what downcast means.

clue.text: The top 2 or 3

definitions.meaning: the highest part of the head or a hill
the answers to 2 and 3 Down, a ruler or sovereign, stand for the monarchy

explanation.definitionFit: It is the summit of something, and also the monarch or monarchy, as in property of the state.

clue.text: Comatose snake takes shelter inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for shelter within the word for snake, which takes it in

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A motionless snake crawls under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... inside' signals the container; 'Comatose' slightly overstates sleep, but both mean unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone comatose is deeply unconscious, much as a sleeper is, so the loose sense is unconscious or dormant.

clue.text: The Spanish, Italian and English are the best

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article

explanation.surface: A claim that Spain, Italy and England top the rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish' means the word for 'the' in Spanish, EL; IT is a crossword abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is the select few regarded as superior, the cream of a group.

clue.text: Some wealth used in this way

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some money was spent like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'wealth' into 'used'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this manner or like so.

clue.text: It provides music room with circular end

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
the round letter O forms the circular end of the word

explanation.surface: A music room is described as having a curved end wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular end' gives O, the round letter, placed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large bowed string instrument, something that produces music when played.

clue.text: White rose developed another way

indicators.note: developed here means changed or evolved, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A white rose grew in a different fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' is the anagram signal on WHITE ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in a different manner or by different means.

clue.text: Poor love, having something to eat in the office

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: in places the meal inside the name of the church service

parts.note: Nones is one of the canonical hours, the daily services or offices of the Church, said at the ninth hour
supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A poor dear has to eat lunch at their desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' is the church sense, the service of the ninth hour, not a workplace; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on your uppers is to be very poor, as if your shoes are worn down to the uppers.
